{"number":1013,"title":"Rename the code phase to code-work, and stop calling tasks scheduled-only","body":"Closes #1012.

Two owner corrections to the task vocabulary. 135 files, all mechanical except the five compatibility surfaces called out below.

## 1. `prework` → `code_work` / `agentic-work`

A task's two phases are peers. The first runs deterministic code in the executor; the second runs an agent; a task may declare only the first, and many do. `prework` named it for what follows it — the same framing error the 2026-08-06 rename set out to fix and did not: `agent_preprocessing` made the agent the reference point, and `prework` kept it there, just implicitly.

Moved together: declaration fields (`prework` → `code_work`, `prework_timeout` → `code_work_timeout`), engine modules, the check, the wire word, symbols, tests and prose.

## 2. A cadence is one way an occurrence is created, not what a task is

`manual` is a first-class frequency, and work that fires on an event or a force reads the same contract as work that fires nightly. [`packs/core/scheduled-tasks.md`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/claude/vigilant-thompson-isx746/packs/core/scheduled-tasks.md) said "recurring" where it meant "the repo's own", and its cron rule offered the task conversion only to work that already had a cron — so event-driven work read as out of scope. It now says the conversion applies with or without a cadence, and the Actions-only exception is narrowed to the step that genuinely needs the Action's own privileges rather than the whole job.

## The five compatibility surfaces

Both earlier spellings stay accepted; nothing in the fleet has to move on this PR's clock.

| Surface | What it does |
|---|---|
| `normalizeTaskDeclaration` | every legacy key maps **straight to today's name**, so a declaration written for the oldest vocabulary normalizes in one pass rather than chaining |
| `task-declaration-shape` | reports two legacy generations rather than one, each with its own exact rename. This finding is the durable driver for member local packs — which is why neither rename ships a migration note |
| run-record wire word | `code-work`, kebab because the line format's charset (`[a-z-]+`) never admitted an underscore. `preprocess` and `prework` in a job log still parse |
| usage aggregate | its counter keys are those same words and it holds rows written under the old ones. The decode renames them; without that the next encode wrote the count as `null` |
| `engine/scheduler/queue/prework-run.mjs` | kept as a re-export shim — a fielded `core` pack imports that path, and the engine and pack lanes deliver separately (#1004, #1006) |

## Verification

- Full suite: **2097 pass, 0 fail** (`node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')`).
- `check_the_world`: **0 blocking, 57 advisory** — byte-identical to the same run stashed against `main`, so no finding is new.
- `engine/selftest.mjs`: 5 probes passed.
- **See-it-fail on both new guards.** Removing the shim turns `engine-pack-lane-shims.test.mjs` red (it derives fielded imports from trunk history, and needed `--depth=200` to be meaningful — it self-guards on a shallow clone and would otherwise have passed vacuously). Disabling the counter rename writes the historical count as `[3,null,1,0,0]`; two new tests in `usage-format.test.mjs` pin it, including a row carrying both spellings at once.

## Out of scope

`engine/migrations/2026-08-06-prework-rename/` keeps its own wording — it states what that rename did, which has not changed. Its id is likewise still spelled `prework-rename` wherever it is referenced.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.

{"number":1013,"title":"Rename the code phase to code-work, and stop calling tasks scheduled-only","body":"Closes #1012.

Two owner corrections to the task vocabulary. 135 files, all mechanical except the five compatibility surfaces called out below.

## 1. `prework` → `code_work` / `agentic-work`

A task's two phases are peers. The first runs deterministic code in the executor; the second runs an agent; a task may declare only the first, and many do. `prework` named it for what follows it — the same framing error the 2026-08-06 rename set out to fix and did not: `agent_preprocessing` made the agent the reference point, and `prework` kept it there, just implicitly.

Moved together: declaration fields (`prework` → `code_work`, `prework_timeout` → `code_work_timeout`), engine modules, the check, the wire word, symbols, tests and prose.

## 2. A cadence is one way an occurrence is created, not what a task is

`manual` is a first-class frequency, and work that fires on an event or a force reads the same contract as work that fires nightly. [`packs/core/scheduled-tasks.md`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/claude/vigilant-thompson-isx746/packs/core/scheduled-tasks.md) said "recurring" where it meant "the repo's own", and its cron rule offered the task conversion only to work that already had a cron — so event-driven work read as out of scope. It now says the conversion applies with or without a cadence, and the Actions-only exception is narrowed to the step that genuinely needs the Action's own privileges rather than the whole job.

## The five compatibility surfaces

Both earlier spellings stay accepted; nothing in the fleet has to move on this PR's clock.

| Surface | What it does |
|---|---|
| `normalizeTaskDeclaration` | every legacy key maps **straight to today's name**, so a declaration written for the oldest vocabulary normalizes in one pass rather than chaining |
| `task-declaration-shape` | reports two legacy generations rather than one, each with its own exact rename. This finding is the durable driver for member local packs — which is why neither rename ships a migration note |
| run-record wire word | `code-work`, kebab because the line format's charset (`[a-z-]+`) never admitted an underscore. `preprocess` and `prework` in a job log still parse |
| usage aggregate | its counter keys are those same words and it holds rows written under the old ones. The decode renames them; without that the next encode wrote the count as `null` |
| `engine/scheduler/queue/prework-run.mjs` | kept as a re-export shim — a fielded `core` pack imports that path, and the engine and pack lanes deliver separately (#1004, #1006) |

## Verification

- Full suite: **2097 pass, 0 fail** (`node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')`).
- `check_the_world`: **0 blocking, 57 advisory** — byte-identical to the same run stashed against `main`, so no finding is new.
- `engine/selftest.mjs`: 5 probes passed.
- **See-it-fail on both new guards.** Removing the shim turns `engine-pack-lane-shims.test.mjs` red (it derives fielded imports from trunk history, and needed `--depth=200` to be meaningful — it self-guards on a shallow clone and would otherwise have passed vacuously). Disabling the counter rename writes the historical count as `[3,null,1,0,0]`; two new tests in `usage-format.test.mjs` pin it, including a row carrying both spellings at once.

## Out of scope

`engine/migrations/2026-08-06-prework-rename/` keeps its own wording — it states what that rename did, which has not changed. Its id is likewise still spelled `prework-rename` wherever it is referenced.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.

{"number":1013,"title":"Rename the code phase to code-work, and stop calling tasks scheduled-only","body":"Closes #1012.

Two owner corrections to the task vocabulary. 135 files, all mechanical except the five compatibility surfaces called out below.

## 1. `prework` → `code_work` / `agentic-work`

A task's two phases are peers. The first runs deterministic code in the executor; the second runs an agent; a task may declare only the first, and many do. `prework` named it for what follows it — the same framing error the 2026-08-06 rename set out to fix and did not: `agent_preprocessing` made the agent the reference point, and `prework` kept it there, just implicitly.

Moved together: declaration fields (`prework` → `code_work`, `prework_timeout` → `code_work_timeout`), engine modules, the check, the wire word, symbols, tests and prose.

## 2. A cadence is one way an occurrence is created, not what a task is

`manual` is a first-class frequency, and work that fires on an event or a force reads the same contract as work that fires nightly. [`packs/core/scheduled-tasks.md`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/claude/vigilant-thompson-isx746/packs/core/scheduled-tasks.md) said "recurring" where it meant "the repo's own", and its cron rule offered the task conversion only to work that already had a cron — so event-driven work read as out of scope. It now says the conversion applies with or without a cadence, and the Actions-only exception is narrowed to the step that genuinely needs the Action's own privileges rather than the whole job.

## The five compatibility surfaces

Both earlier spellings stay accepted; nothing in the fleet has to move on this PR's clock.

| Surface | What it does |
|---|---|
| `normalizeTaskDeclaration` | every legacy key maps **straight to today's name**, so a declaration written for the oldest vocabulary normalizes in one pass rather than chaining |
| `task-declaration-shape` | reports two legacy generations rather than one, each with its own exact rename. This finding is the durable driver for member local packs — which is why neither rename ships a migration note |
| run-record wire word | `code-work`, kebab because the line format's charset (`[a-z-]+`) never admitted an underscore. `preprocess` and `prework` in a job log still parse |
| usage aggregate | its counter keys are those same words and it holds rows written under the old ones. The decode renames them; without that the next encode wrote the count as `null` |
| `engine/scheduler/queue/prework-run.mjs` | kept as a re-export shim — a fielded `core` pack imports that path, and the engine and pack lanes deliver separately (#1004, #1006) |

## Verification

- Full suite: **2097 pass, 0 fail** (`node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')`).
- `check_the_world`: **0 blocking, 57 advisory** — byte-identical to the same run stashed against `main`, so no finding is new.
- `engine/selftest.mjs`: 5 probes passed.
- **See-it-fail on both new guards.** Removing the shim turns `engine-pack-lane-shims.test.mjs` red (it derives fielded imports from trunk history, and needed `--depth=200` to be meaningful — it self-guards on a shallow clone and would otherwise have passed vacuously). Disabling the counter rename writes the historical count as `[3,null,1,0,0]`; two new tests in `usage-format.test.mjs` pin it, including a row carrying both spellings at once.

## Out of scope

`engine/migrations/2026-08-06-prework-rename/` keeps its own wording — it states what that rename did, which has not changed. Its id is likewise still spelled `prework-rename` wherever it is referenced.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.

{"number":1013,"title":"Rename the code phase to code-work, and stop calling tasks scheduled-only","body":"Closes #1012.

Two owner corrections to the task vocabulary. 135 files, all mechanical except the five compatibility surfaces called out below.

## 1. `prework` → `code_work` / `agentic-work`

A task's two phases are peers. The first runs deterministic code in the executor; the second runs an agent; a task may declare only the first, and many do. `prework` named it for what follows it — the same framing error the 2026-08-06 rename set out to fix and did not: `agent_preprocessing` made the agent the reference point, and `prework` kept it there, just implicitly.

Moved together: declaration fields (`prework` → `code_work`, `prework_timeout` → `code_work_timeout`), engine modules, the check, the wire word, symbols, tests and prose.

## 2. A cadence is one way an occurrence is created, not what a task is

`manual` is a first-class frequency, and work that fires on an event or a force reads the same contract as work that fires nightly. [`packs/core/scheduled-tasks.md`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/claude/vigilant-thompson-isx746/packs/core/scheduled-tasks.md) said "recurring" where it meant "the repo's own", and its cron rule offered the task conversion only to work that already had a cron — so event-driven work read as out of scope. It now says the conversion applies with or without a cadence, and the Actions-only exception is narrowed to the step that genuinely needs the Action's own privileges rather than the whole job.

## The five compatibility surfaces

Both earlier spellings stay accepted; nothing in the fleet has to move on this PR's clock.

| Surface | What it does |
|---|---|
| `normalizeTaskDeclaration` | every legacy key maps **straight to today's name**, so a declaration written for the oldest vocabulary normalizes in one pass rather than chaining |
| `task-declaration-shape` | reports two legacy generations rather than one, each with its own exact rename. This finding is the durable driver for member local packs — which is why neither rename ships a migration note |
| run-record wire word | `code-work`, kebab because the line format's charset (`[a-z-]+`) never admitted an underscore. `preprocess` and `prework` in a job log still parse |
| usage aggregate | its counter keys are those same words and it holds rows written under the old ones. The decode renames them; without that the next encode wrote the count as `null` |
| `engine/scheduler/queue/prework-run.mjs` | kept as a re-export shim — a fielded `core` pack imports that path, and the engine and pack lanes deliver separately (#1004, #1006) |

## Verification

- Full suite: **2097 pass, 0 fail** (`node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')`).
- `check_the_world`: **0 blocking, 57 advisory** — byte-identical to the same run stashed against `main`, so no finding is new.
- `engine/selftest.mjs`: 5 probes passed.
- **See-it-fail on both new guards.** Removing the shim turns `engine-pack-lane-shims.test.mjs` red (it derives fielded imports from trunk history, and needed `--depth=200` to be meaningful — it self-guards on a shallow clone and would otherwise have passed vacuously). Disabling the counter rename writes the historical count as `[3,null,1,0,0]`; two new tests in `usage-format.test.mjs` pin it, including a row carrying both spellings at once.

## Out of scope

`engine/migrations/2026-08-06-prework-rename/` keeps its own wording — it states what that rename did, which has not changed. Its id is likewise still spelled `prework-rename` wherever it is referenced.

{"number":1013,"title":"Rename the code phase to code-work, and stop calling tasks scheduled-only","body":"Closes #1012.

Two owner corrections to the task vocabulary. 135 files, all mechanical except the five compatibility surfaces called out below.

## 1. `prework` → `code_work` / `agentic-work`

A task's two phases are peers. The first runs deterministic code in the executor; the second runs an agent; a task may declare only the first, and many do. `prework` named it for what follows it — the same framing error the 2026-08-06 rename set out to fix and did not: `agent_preprocessing` made the agent the reference point, and `prework` kept it there, just implicitly.

Moved together: declaration fields (`prework` → `code_work`, `prework_timeout` → `code_work_timeout`), engine modules, the check, the wire word, symbols, tests and prose.

## 2. A cadence is one way an occurrence is created, not what a task is

`manual` is a first-class frequency, and work that fires on an event or a force reads the same contract as work that fires nightly. [`packs/core/scheduled-tasks.md`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/claude/vigilant-thompson-isx746/packs/core/scheduled-tasks.md) said "recurring" where it meant "the repo's own", and its cron rule offered the task conversion only to work that already had a cron — so event-driven work read as out of scope. It now says the conversion applies with or without a cadence, and the Actions-only exception is narrowed to the step that genuinely needs the Action's own privileges rather than the whole job.

## The five compatibility surfaces

Both earlier spellings stay accepted; nothing in the fleet has to move on this PR's clock.

| Surface | What it does |
|---|---|
| `normalizeTaskDeclaration` | every legacy key maps **straight to today's name**, so a declaration written for the oldest vocabulary normalizes in one pass rather than chaining |
| `task-declaration-shape` | reports two legacy generations rather than one, each with its own exact rename. This finding is the durable driver for member local packs — which is why neither rename ships a migration note |
| run-record wire word | `code-work`, kebab because the line format's charset (`[a-z-]+`) never admitted an underscore. `preprocess` and `prework` in a job log still parse |
| usage aggregate | its counter keys are those same words and it holds rows written under the old ones. The decode renames them; without that the next encode wrote the count as `null` |
| `engine/scheduler/queue/prework-run.mjs` | kept as a re-export shim — a fielded `core` pack imports that path, and the engine and pack lanes deliver separately (#1004, #1006) |

## Verification

- Full suite: **2097 pass, 0 fail** (`node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')`).
- `check_the_world`: **0 blocking, 57 advisory** — byte-identical to the same run stashed against `main`, so no finding is new.
- `engine/selftest.mjs`: 5 probes passed.
- **See-it-fail on both new guards.** Removing the shim turns `engine-pack-lane-shims.test.mjs` red (it derives fielded imports from trunk history, and needed `--depth=200` to be meaningful — it self-guards on a shallow clone and would otherwise have passed vacuously). Disabling the counter rename writes the historical count as `[3,null,1,0,0]`; two new tests in `usage-format.test.mjs` pin it, including a row carrying both spellings at once.

## Out of scope

`engine/migrations/2026-08-06-prework-rename/` keeps its own wording — it states what that rename did, which has not changed. Its id is likewise still spelled `prework-rename` wherever it is referenced.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.

Two owner corrections to the task vocabulary. 135 files, all mechanical except the five compatibility surfaces called out below.

## 1. `prework` → `code_work` / `agentic-work`

A task's two phases are peers. The first runs deterministic code in the executor; the second runs an agent; a task may declare only the first, and many do. `prework` named it for what follows it — the same framing error the 2026-08-06 rename set out to fix and did not: `agent_preprocessing` made the agent the reference point, and `prework` kept it there, just implicitly.

Moved together: declaration fields (`prework` → `code_work`, `prework_timeout` → `code_work_timeout`), engine modules, the check, the wire word, symbols, tests and prose.

## 2. A cadence is one way an occurrence is created, not what a task is

`manual` is a first-class frequency, and work that fires on an event or a force reads the same contract as work that fires nightly. [`packs/core/scheduled-tasks.md`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/claude/vigilant-thompson-isx746/packs/core/scheduled-tasks.md) said "recurring" where it meant "the repo's own", and its cron rule offered the task conversion only to work that already had a cron — so event-driven work read as out of scope. It now says the conversion applies with or without a cadence, and the Actions-only exception is narrowed to the step that genuinely needs the Action's own privileges rather than the whole job.

## The five compatibility surfaces

Both earlier spellings stay accepted; nothing in the fleet has to move on this PR's clock.

| Surface | What it does |
|---|---|
| `normalizeTaskDeclaration` | every legacy key maps **straight to today's name**, so a declaration written for the oldest vocabulary normalizes in one pass rather than chaining |
| `task-declaration-shape` | reports two legacy generations rather than one, each with its own exact rename. This finding is the durable driver for member local packs — which is why neither rename ships a migration note |
| run-record wire word | `code-work`, kebab because the line format's charset (`[a-z-]+`) never admitted an underscore. `preprocess` and `prework` in a job log still parse |
| usage aggregate | its counter keys are those same words and it holds rows written under the old ones. The decode renames them; without that the next encode wrote the count as `null` |
| `engine/scheduler/queue/prework-run.mjs` | kept as a re-export shim — a fielded `core` pack imports that path, and the engine and pack lanes deliver separately (#1004, #1006) |

## Verification

- Full suite: **2097 pass, 0 fail** (`node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')`).
- `check_the_world`: **0 blocking, 57 advisory** — byte-identical to the same run stashed against `main`, so no finding is new.
- `engine/selftest.mjs`: 5 probes passed.
- **See-it-fail on both new guards.** Removing the shim turns `engine-pack-lane-shims.test.mjs` red (it derives fielded imports from trunk history, and needed `--depth=200` to be meaningful — it self-guards on a shallow clone and would otherwise have passed vacuously). Disabling the counter rename writes the historical count as `[3,null,1,0,0]`; two new tests in `usage-format.test.mjs` pin it, including a row carrying both spellings at once.

## Out of scope

`engine/migrations/2026-08-06-prework-rename/` keeps its own wording — it states what that rename did, which has not changed. Its id is likewise still spelled `prework-rename` wherever it is referenced.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.

- session-start-hook: Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code on the web. Use when the user wants to set up a repository for Claude Code on the web, create a SessionStart hook to ensure their project can run tests and linters during web sessions.
- adopt-claudinite: Bootstrap Claudinite into a consuming repo — mount, hooks, checks, skills. Use when asked to bootstrap, adopt, or set up Claudinite, or to baseline a repo to pick up updates.
- adopt-pack: Add one or more packs to an already-adopted Claudinite member — declare, run each pack's adoption interview, re-vendor, scaffold, land. Use when asked to adopt, add, enable, or declare a pack (e.g. product-wiki, executable-requirements) on a repo that already runs Claudinite.
- authoring-agent-docs: How to write instruction files coding agents follow reliably. Use before writing or editing any Claude instruction doc — a project CLAUDE.md, a convention doc, a routine spec.
- bug-investigation: Method for investigating a bug and pinning down its root cause. Use when investigating a bug report, when a fix didn't hold or a bug recurs, or when a report doesn't reproduce against main.
- bump-version: Raise the project's version — a minor bump by default. Use when the owner says "bump version".
- ci-performance-evaluation: Method for finding where a repo's CI time actually goes and what is worth fixing. Use when CI feels slow, when investigating a runtime regression, or when the weekly ci-performance task hands you a finding.
- extract-from-activity: Mine a window of a repo's commits, merged PRs and issue activity for durable, reusable lessons and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from repo artifacts — the growth-extract task's activity half, or an owner asking what a recent stretch of work taught.
- extract-from-conversations: Mine an agent-user conversation — a captured conversation log or the live session — for friction-driven lessons (misunderstandings, backtracks, measured wall-time waits) and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from a session transcript or the conversation-logs branch, or when an owner asks for a retrospective.
- file-placement: Where a file should live — the reference-distance metric, the high-reach code smell, and the mandated-location, test-location and plugin-contract exemptions. Use before placing, moving, or renaming a file, or when reviewing where one lives.
- generate-project-instructions: Decompose a project into its pack facets (working-style class, technology, aspect, domain) and extract its working instructions into reusable canon packs plus the project's own local packs (.claudinite/local_packs/). Use when a project has no established working style yet, or it exhibits a facet no pack covers — during bootstrap of a fresh/empty repo, or on an uplevel request.
- github-actions-scheduling: What a GitHub Actions `schedule:` trigger actually guarantees — late fires, dropped fires, the 60-day disable — and how to build and describe scheduled work around it. Use when adding, changing, explaining, or debugging anything that runs on a cron in GitHub Actions.
- growth-dedup: Prune a repo's local packs of items the mounted Claudinite canon now covers — remove, strip to residue, or track a wording drift, never grow an entry. Use when the growth dedup task runs, or when asked to reconcile or dedup local packs against the canon.
- prose-to-checks: Mine pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. Use when auditing packs for convertible rules, when the weekly prose-to-checks sweep runs, or as the upgrade pass over prose a growth-extract run just wrote.
- repo-text-sweeps: Mechanics for grep/sed sweeps, renames, and path relocations across a repo. Use before a bulk find-replace, a rename, or moving files — and after one, to catch silently broken references.
- single-branch-status: Assess one branch's landed status — merged, already-in-main, superseded, orphaned, or genuine unmerged work — read-only. Use when triaging whether a single branch is safe to delete, judging by content not the ref's name (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-branches task hands you branches to assess).
- single-issue-triage: Triage one open issue and take the first applicable action — close-if-implemented, needs-decision, blocked, quick-win, or leave. Use when acting on a single issue; "implemented in main" must be verified against main's current content and the default is to comment, not close (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-issues task hands you issues to triage).
- single-pr-status: Assess one open pull request's landed status — keep-open, or closeable (merged, already-in-main, superseded, stale) — read-only. Use when triaging whether a single PR should stay open, judging by its commits and diff not its title (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-prs task hands you PRs to assess).
- unattended-agents: Architecture and practices for unattended, automation-invoked agents and recurring routines. Use when building, structuring, or running an AI agent, a scheduled routine, or a multi-stage agent pipeline.
- writing-claudinite-skills: Authoring or changing a skill in the Claudinite corpus — SKILL.md conventions, where a skill's checks and tests live, catalog and pack wiring. Use when creating or editing a pack's skills/<name>/ in the canon; a consumer project's own agent docs are authoring-agent-docs' turf.
- writing-migration-plans: How to order the phases of an implementation or migration plan so nothing stalls mid-run — front-load the out-of-band setup, collapse the review gates into one stacked-PR pass, leave only executable steps — and how to keep its tracking issue append-only while implementing. Use when writing or reviewing a migration plan or a phased implementation plan, and when working through one's tracking issue.
- writing-tests: Practices for writing tests you can trust. Use before writing or changing any test — see-it-fail discipline, snapshot/golden rules, CI-only and heavy-browser tests, fuzzy-metric gating.
- design: Create a design canvas — a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including Markdown ones — format is part of the design pass, never a speed shortcut.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, handing the viewer a file to save, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation

{"number":1013,"title":"Rename the code phase to code-work, and stop calling tasks scheduled-only","body":"Closes #1012.

Two owner corrections to the task vocabulary. 135 files, all mechanical except the five compatibility surfaces called out below.

## 1. `prework` → `code_work` / `agentic-work`

A task's two phases are peers. The first runs deterministic code in the executor; the second runs an agent; a task may declare only the first, and many do. `prework` named it for what follows it — the same framing error the 2026-08-06 rename set out to fix and did not: `agent_preprocessing` made the agent the reference point, and `prework` kept it there, just implicitly.

Moved together: declaration fields (`prework` → `code_work`, `prework_timeout` → `code_work_timeout`), engine modules, the check, the wire word, symbols, tests and prose.

## 2. A cadence is one way an occurrence is created, not what a task is

`manual` is a first-class frequency, and work that fires on an event or a force reads the same contract as work that fires nightly. [`packs/core/scheduled-tasks.md`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/claude/vigilant-thompson-isx746/packs/core/scheduled-tasks.md) said "recurring" where it meant "the repo's own", and its cron rule offered the task conversion only to work that already had a cron — so event-driven work read as out of scope. It now says the conversion applies with or without a cadence, and the Actions-only exception is narrowed to the step that genuinely needs the Action's own privileges rather than the whole job.

## The five compatibility surfaces

Both earlier spellings stay accepted; nothing in the fleet has to move on this PR's clock.

| Surface | What it does |
|---|---|
| `normalizeTaskDeclaration` | every legacy key maps **straight to today's name**, so a declaration written for the oldest vocabulary normalizes in one pass rather than chaining |
| `task-declaration-shape` | reports two legacy generations rather than one, each with its own exact rename. This finding is the durable driver for member local packs — which is why neither rename ships a migration note |
| run-record wire word | `code-work`, kebab because the line format's charset (`[a-z-]+`) never admitted an underscore. `preprocess` and `prework` in a job log still parse |
| usage aggregate | its counter keys are those same words and it holds rows written under the old ones. The decode renames them; without that the next encode wrote the count as `null` |
| `engine/scheduler/queue/prework-run.mjs` | kept as a re-export shim — a fielded `core` pack imports that path, and the engine and pack lanes deliver separately (#1004, #1006) |

## Verification

- Full suite: **2097 pass, 0 fail** (`node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')`).
- `check_the_world`: **0 blocking, 57 advisory** — byte-identical to the same run stashed against `main`, so no finding is new.
- `engine/selftest.mjs`: 5 probes passed.
- **See-it-fail on both new guards.** Removing the shim turns `engine-pack-lane-shims.test.mjs` red (it derives fielded imports from trunk history, and needed `--depth=200` to be meaningful — it self-guards on a shallow clone and would otherwise have passed vacuously). Disabling the counter rename writes the historical count as `[3,null,1,0,0]`; two new tests in `usage-format.test.mjs` pin it, including a row carrying both spellings at once.

## Out of scope

`engine/migrations/2026-08-06-prework-rename/` keeps its own wording — it states what that rename did, which has not changed. Its id is likewise still spelled `prework-rename` wherever it is referenced.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.

{"number":1013,"title":"Rename the code phase to code-work, and stop calling tasks scheduled-only","body":"Closes #1012.

Two owner corrections to the task vocabulary. 135 files, all mechanical except the five compatibility surfaces called out below.

## 1. `prework` → `code_work` / `agentic-work`

A task's two phases are peers. The first runs deterministic code in the executor; the second runs an agent; a task may declare only the first, and many do. `prework` named it for what follows it — the same framing error the 2026-08-06 rename set out to fix and did not: `agent_preprocessing` made the agent the reference point, and `prework` kept it there, just implicitly.

Moved together: declaration fields (`prework` → `code_work`, `prework_timeout` → `code_work_timeout`), engine modules, the check, the wire word, symbols, tests and prose.

## 2. A cadence is one way an occurrence is created, not what a task is

`manual` is a first-class frequency, and work that fires on an event or a force reads the same contract as work that fires nightly. [`packs/core/scheduled-tasks.md`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/claude/vigilant-thompson-isx746/packs/core/scheduled-tasks.md) said "recurring" where it meant "the repo's own", and its cron rule offered the task conversion only to work that already had a cron — so event-driven work read as out of scope. It now says the conversion applies with or without a cadence, and the Actions-only exception is narrowed to the step that genuinely needs the Action's own privileges rather than the whole job.

## The five compatibility surfaces

Both earlier spellings stay accepted; nothing in the fleet has to move on this PR's clock.

| Surface | What it does |
|---|---|
| `normalizeTaskDeclaration` | every legacy key maps **straight to today's name**, so a declaration written for the oldest vocabulary normalizes in one pass rather than chaining |
| `task-declaration-shape` | reports two legacy generations rather than one, each with its own exact rename. This finding is the durable driver for member local packs — which is why neither rename ships a migration note |
| run-record wire word | `code-work`, kebab because the line format's charset (`[a-z-]+`) never admitted an underscore. `preprocess` and `prework` in a job log still parse |
| usage aggregate | its counter keys are those same words and it holds rows written under the old ones. The decode renames them; without that the next encode wrote the count as `null` |
| `engine/scheduler/queue/prework-run.mjs` | kept as a re-export shim — a fielded `core` pack imports that path, and the engine and pack lanes deliver separately (#1004, #1006) |

## Verification

- Full suite: **2097 pass, 0 fail** (`node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')`).
- `check_the_world`: **0 blocking, 57 advisory** — byte-identical to the same run stashed against `main`, so no finding is new.
- `engine/selftest.mjs`: 5 probes passed.
- **See-it-fail on both new guards.** Removing the shim turns `engine-pack-lane-shims.test.mjs` red (it derives fielded imports from trunk history, and needed `--depth=200` to be meaningful — it self-guards on a shallow clone and would otherwise have passed vacuously). Disabling the counter rename writes the historical count as `[3,null,1,0,0]`; two new tests in `usage-format.test.mjs` pin it, including a row carrying both spellings at once.

## Out of scope

`engine/migrations/2026-08-06-prework-rename/` keeps its own wording — it states what that rename did, which has not changed. Its id is likewise still spelled `prework-rename` wherever it is referenced.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.

- growth-dedup: Prune a repo's local packs of items the mounted Claudinite canon now covers — remove, strip to residue, or track a wording drift, never grow an entry. Use when the growth dedup task runs, or when asked to reconcile or dedup local packs against the canon.
- prose-to-checks: Mine pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. {"number":1013,"title":"Rename the code phase to code-work, and stop calling tasks scheduled-only","body":"Closes #1012.

Two owner corrections to the task vocabulary. 135 files, all mechanical except the five compatibility surfaces called out below.

## 1. `prework` → `code_work` / `agentic-work`

A task's two phases are peers. The first runs deterministic code in the executor; the second runs an agent; a task may declare only the first, and many do. `prework` named it for what follows it — the same framing error the 2026-08-06 rename set out to fix and did not: `agent_preprocessing` made the agent the reference point, and `prework` kept it there, just implicitly.

Moved together: declaration fields (`prework` → `code_work`, `prework_timeout` → `code_work_timeout`), engine modules, the check, the wire word, symbols, tests and prose.

## 2. A cadence is one way an occurrence is created, not what a task is

`manual` is a first-class frequency, and work that fires on an event or a force reads the same contract as work that fires nightly. [`packs/core/scheduled-tasks.md`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/claude/vigilant-thompson-isx746/packs/core/scheduled-tasks.md) said "recurring" where it meant "the repo's own", and its cron rule offered the task conversion only to work that already had a cron — so event-driven work read as out of scope. It now says the conversion applies with or without a cadence, and the Actions-only exception is narrowed to the step that genuinely needs the Action's own privileges rather than the whole job.

## The five compatibility surfaces

Both earlier spellings stay accepted; nothing in the fleet has to move on this PR's clock.

| Surface | What it does |
|---|---|
| `normalizeTaskDeclaration` | every legacy key maps **straight to today's name**, so a declaration written for the oldest vocabulary normalizes in one pass rather than chaining |
| `task-declaration-shape` | reports two legacy generations rather than one, each with its own exact rename. This finding is the durable driver for member local packs — which is why neither rename ships a migration note |
| run-record wire word | `code-work`, kebab because the line format's charset (`[a-z-]+`) never admitted an underscore. `preprocess` and `prework` in a job log still parse |
| usage aggregate | its counter keys are those same words and it holds rows written under the old ones. The decode renames them; without that the next encode wrote the count as `null` |
| `engine/scheduler/queue/prework-run.mjs` | kept as a re-export shim — a fielded `core` pack imports that path, and the engine and pack lanes deliver separately (#1004, #1006) |

## Verification

- Full suite: **2097 pass, 0 fail** (`node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')`).
- `check_the_world`: **0 blocking, 57 advisory** — byte-identical to the same run stashed against `main`, so no finding is new.
- `engine/selftest.mjs`: 5 probes passed.
- **See-it-fail on both new guards.** Removing the shim turns `engine-pack-lane-shims.test.mjs` red (it derives fielded imports from trunk history, and needed `--depth=200` to be meaningful — it self-guards on a shallow clone and would otherwise have passed vacuously). Disabling the counter rename writes the historical count as `[3,null,1,0,0]`; two new tests in `usage-format.test.mjs` pin it, including a row carrying both spellings at once.

## Out of scope

`engine/migrations/2026-08-06-prework-rename/` keeps its own wording — it states what that rename did, which has not changed. Its id is likewise still spelled `prework-rename` wherever it is referenced.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.

input.command:
cd /home/user/Claudinite
python3 - <<'PY'
import re, subprocess, os

# Inside PROSE, the phase is spelled code-work. These forms are the FIELD and keep
# the underscore: the timeout field, a backticked or quoted key, a declaration
# `code_work:`, and a property access `.code_work`.
FIELD = re.compile(r'code_work_timeout|`code_work`|"code_work"|\'code_work\'|code_work:|\.code_work\b')
TOK = '\x00F%d\x00'

def prose_fix(s):
    saved = []
    def stash(m):
        saved.append(m.group(0))
        return TOK % (len(saved) - 1)
    s = FIELD.sub(stash, s)
    s = re.sub(r'\bcode_work\b', 'code-work', s)
    for i, v in enumerate(saved):
        s = s.replace(TOK % i, v)
    return s

changed = []
for p in subprocess.run(['git','ls-files','*.mjs','*.yml'],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout.split():
    if not os.path.exists(p): continue
    s = open(p).read()
    if 'code_work' not in s: continue
    out = []
    for line in s.split('\n'):
        # comment lines only — code keeps the field spelling

input.command:
cd /home/user/Claudinite
git add -A && git commit -q -m "Spell the phase code-work in prose, code_work only as the field

The rename split the two spellings by FILE TYPE — .md got the prose word, every
other file got the field word — so prose living inside .mjs comments and inside
JSON string values came out wearing the field's underscore. The owner caught it
on a waiver reason in .claudinite-checks.json.

The rule is about the token, not the file: code_work is the declaration field
(beside agent_model, expected_outcome) and keeps the underscore wherever it names
that field, backticked, quoted, followed by a colon, or as .code_work; everything
else reads code-work. Applied to comment lines, two JSON prose strings, and the
strings a human actually reads — a triage issue's \"code-work exited 1\" and the
work item's delivered-artifacts heading.

That heading is also MATCHED, not just written: withSection locates the section
it already wrote so a re-entrant run updates it in place. Renaming it alone would
have appended a second section to every in-flight item carrying the old one, so
the heading is now a shared constant with its two earlier spellings beside it,
and withSection takes aliases to find a section under any of them. Proven by
removing the alias lookup and watching the new test report two sections.

The rename edits six pack directories, and a member receives a pack directory
only when the canon's version exceeds the one it holds — so without the bump
the rename reaches nobody while CI reports it shipped.

The sim README's link to github-actions-scheduling was written against the
per-session flat `.claude/skills/` mount, which only exists inside a session
and dangles from the tracked tree. It now points at the skill's real home
under the pack that owns it. The link was already wrong on main; this change
put the file in the work scope, which is what surfaced it.

the code phase to code-work, and stop calling tasks scheduled-only

Two owner corrections to the task vocabulary.

A task's two phases are peers. The first runs deterministic code in the
executor; the second runs an agent; a task may declare only the first, and
many do. `prework` named it for what follows it, which is the same framing
error the 2026-08-06 rename set out to fix and did not — `agent_preprocessing`
made the agent the reference point, and `prework` kept it there, just
implicitly. `code_work` names the phase for what it is, beside `agentic-work`.

The declaration fields, the engine modules, the check, the wire word and the
prose all move together. Both earlier spellings stay accepted:

- `normalizeTaskDeclaration` maps every legacy key straight to today's name,
  so a declaration written for the oldest vocabulary normalizes in one pass.
- `task-declaration-shape` now reports two legacy generations rather than one,
  each with its own exact rename. That finding is the durable driver for
  member local packs, which is why neither rename ships a migration note.
- The run-record wire word is `code-work`, kebab because the line format's
  charset never admitted an underscore; `preprocess` and `prework` in a job
  log still parse.
- The usage aggregate's counter keys are those same words, and it holds rows
  written under the old ones. Its decode renames them instead of letting the
  next encode drop the count to null, which is what happened before the fix.
- `engine/scheduler/queue/prework-run.mjs` stays as a shim: a fielded `core`
  pack imports that path, and the engine and pack lanes deliver separately.

On the second correction: a cadence is one way an occurrence gets created,
not what a task is. `manual` is a first-class frequency, and work that fires
on an event or a force reads the same contract as work that fires nightly.
The core contract said "recurring" where it meant "the repo's own", and its
cron rule offered the conversion only to work that already had a cron.

The 2026-08-06 migration record keeps its own wording — it states what that
rename did, which has not changed.

Refs #1012

The sim README's link to github-actions-scheduling was written against the
per-session flat `.claude/skills/` mount, which only exists inside a session
and dangles from the tracked tree. It now points at the skill's real home
under the pack that owns it. The link was already wrong on main; this change
put the file in the work scope, which is what surfaced it.

the code phase to code-work, and stop calling tasks scheduled-only

Two owner corrections to the task vocabulary.

A task's two phases are peers. The first runs deterministic code in the
executor; the second runs an agent; a task may declare only the first, and
many do. `prework` named it for what follows it, which is the same framing
error the 2026-08-06 rename set out to fix and did not — `agent_preprocessing`
made the agent the reference point, and `prework` kept it there, just
implicitly. `code_work` names the phase for what it is, beside `agentic-work`.

The declaration fields, the engine modules, the check, the wire word and the
prose all move together. Both earlier spellings stay accepted:

- `normalizeTaskDeclaration` maps every legacy key straight to today's name,
  so a declaration written for the oldest vocabulary normalizes in one pass.
- `task-declaration-shape` now reports two legacy generations rather than one,
  each with its own exact rename. That finding is the durable driver for
  member local packs, which is why neither rename ships a migration note.
- The run-record wire word is `code-work`, kebab because the line format's
  charset never admitted an underscore; `preprocess` and `prework` in a job
  log still parse.
- The usage aggregate's counter keys are those same words, and it holds rows
  written under the old ones. Its decode renames them instead of letting the
  next encode drop the count to null, which is what happened before the fix.
- `engine/scheduler/queue/prework-run.mjs` stays as a shim: a fielded `core`
  pack imports that path, and the engine and pack lanes deliver separately.

On the second correction: a cadence is one way an occurrence gets created,
not what a task is. `manual` is a first-class frequency, and work that fires
on an event or a force reads the same contract as work that fires nightly.
The core contract said "recurring" where it meant "the repo's own", and its
cron rule offered the conversion only to work that already had a cron.

The 2026-08-06 migration record keeps its own wording — it states what that
rename did, which has not changed.

Refs #1012

You were right that something was off, though not quite in the way the question implied — I hadn't claimed a blanket `code-work`. The split I chose is `code_work` for the declaration field (matching `agent_model`, `expected_outcome`) and `code-work` everywhere else. What broke is that my sweep decided which was which **by file extension**: `.md` got prose, every other file got the field spelling. So prose inside `.mjs` comments and inside JSON strings — like that waiver reason — came out wearing the underscore. 42 files' worth.

Chasing it surfaced something worse than spelling. Three of those strings aren't comments, they're rendered into GitHub issue bodies, and one of them — `### Delivered by code_work` — is also **matched**: `withSection` finds the section it previously wrote so a re-entrant code-work run updates it in place. Renaming it alone would have appended a second section to every in-flight work item carrying the old heading. It's now a shared constant with both earlier spellings beside it as aliases, and I confirmed the guard bites by removing the alias lookup and watching the new test report two sections.

The rename split the two spellings by FILE TYPE — .md got the prose word, every
other file got the field word — so prose living inside .mjs comments and inside
JSON string values came out wearing the field's underscore. The owner caught it
on a waiver reason in .claudinite-checks.json.

The rule is about the token, not the file: code_work is the declaration field
(beside agent_model, expected_outcome) and keeps the underscore wherever it names
that field, backticked, quoted, followed by a colon, or as .code_work; everything
else reads code-work. Applied to comment lines, two JSON prose strings, and the
strings a human actually reads — a triage issue's "code-work exited 1" and the
work item's delivered-artifacts heading.

That heading is also MATCHED, not just written: withSection locates the section
it already wrote so a re-entrant run updates it in place. Renaming it alone would
have appended a second section to every in-flight item carrying the old one, so
the heading is now a shared constant with its two earlier spellings beside it,
and withSection takes aliases to find a section under any of them. Proven by
removing the alias lookup and watching the new test report two sections.

Refs #1012

content.content:
---
name: merge-to-main
description: Merge the change in front of the owner into main. Use when the owner says "LGTM" or asks to merge/land the current branch or PR into main.
---


The portable recipe for landing the change in front of the owner on `main` — the *mechanics* behind the owner's merge-to-main command (the owner's preferences own the trigger *phrase*; this file owns the *how*). Invoked through the `merge-to-main` skill (this skill); this doc stays the canonical recipe.

**A project's bespoke merge policy overrides this default.** Most projects need nothing here — this default is the whole story. A project that genuinely diverges (a different merge method, a CI/twice-green gate, an extra approval) **states so by naming its merge-policy file explicitly in its own `CLAUDE.md`**. When that declaration is present, read that file first and let it override the divergent points below; when it's absent, follow this default as-is. Don't go hunting for a policy file that the project's `CLAUDE.md` doesn't name.

## Recipe (~4 calls)

1. Load both GitHub tools in **one** `ToolSearch`: `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request`.
2. No PR open for the branch yet? `create_pull_request` (base `main`); end the body with `Closes #<issue>`, and take the PR number from the returned URL.
3. Gate on CI **only if the repo has it** — a workflow that actually runs on PRs/pushes. `workflow_call`-only reusable workflows (this repo hosts some) are *not* CI: they never run here, so a non-empty `.github/workflows/` alone proves nothing; check the PR for check runs instead. No CI → no gate; don't wait for checks that will never come.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Merge directly — don't pre-read status; the call fails loudly if it isn't mergeable.
5. Sync local `main`: `git checkout main && git pull origin main`.

The two divergent points — **`squash`** as the method and **CI gating** — are exactly what a bespoke policy file changes.

## After the merge: capture the conversation (every session, every user)

Once the merge has landed and local `main` is synced, run the growth pack's capture step:
`node .claudinite/shared/packs/grow_with_claudinite/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>` (from the canon repo itself: `node packs/grow_with_claudinite/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`), `<n>` being the issue your `Closes #<issue>` named. Deterministic, seconds-long; it pushes the conversation to the orphan `conversation-logs` branch. It runs **here, in-session, because it needs the live transcript** — the lessons extraction then happens later, in the conversation half of the repo's scheduled `growth-extract` task (MCP-native, with a rethink window), so there is nothing to schedule and no in-session lessons pass ([the pack README](../../../../packs/grow_with_claudinite/README.md) owns the standard). A later merge in the same session just runs capture again — it captures the delta. In the rare repo that removed the `grow_with_claudinite` pack from `.claudinite-checks.json`, skip this step.

## Don't

- **Don't** re-read the issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge; trust it.

the phase code-work in prose, code_work only as the field

The rename split the two spellings by FILE TYPE — .md got the prose word, every
other file got the field word — so prose living inside .mjs comments and inside
JSON string values came out wearing the field's underscore. The owner caught it
on a waiver reason in .claudinite-checks.json.

The rule is about the token, not the file: code_work is the declaration field
(beside agent_model, expected_outcome) and keeps the underscore wherever it names
that field, backticked, quoted, followed by a colon, or as .code_work; everything
else reads code-work. Applied to comment lines, two JSON prose strings, and the
strings a human actually reads — a triage issue's "code-work exited 1" and the
work item's delivered-artifacts heading.

That heading is also MATCHED, not just written: withSection locates the section
it already wrote so a re-entrant run updates it in place. Renaming it alone would
have appended a second section to every in-flight item carrying the old one, so
the heading is now a shared constant with its two earlier spellings beside it,
and withSection takes aliases to find a section under any of them. Proven by
removing the alias lookup and watching the new test report two sections.

Refs #1012

the phase code-work in prose, code_work only as the field

The rename split the two spellings by FILE TYPE — .md got the prose word, every
other file got the field word — so prose living inside .mjs comments and inside
JSON string values came out wearing the field's underscore. The owner caught it
on a waiver reason in .claudinite-checks.json.

The rule is about the token, not the file: code_work is the declaration field
(beside agent_model, expected_outcome) and keeps the underscore wherever it names
that field, backticked, quoted, followed by a colon, or as .code_work; everything
else reads code-work. Applied to comment lines, two JSON prose strings, and the
strings a human actually reads — a triage issue's "code-work exited 1" and the
work item's delivered-artifacts heading.

That heading is also MATCHED, not just written: withSection locates the section
it already wrote so a re-entrant run updates it in place. Renaming it alone would
have appended a second section to every in-flight item carrying the old one, so
the heading is now a shared constant with its two earlier spellings beside it,
and withSection takes aliases to find a section under any of them. Proven by
removing the alias lookup and watching the new test report two sections.

Refs #1012
